A square with side length \(3\) is inscribed in an isosceles triangle with one side of the square along the base of the triangle. A square with side length \(2\) has two vertices on the other square and the other two on sides of the triangle, as shown. What is the area of the triangle?

[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

In square \(ABCD,\) points \(P\) and \(Q\) lie on \(\overline{AD}\) and \(\overline{AB},\) respectively. Segments \(\overline{BP}\) and \(\overline{CQ}\) intersect at right angles at \(R,\) with \(BR = 6\) and \(PR = 7.\) What is the area of the square?

[Figure 1](attached-image-2)

Three identical square sheets of paper each with side length \(6\) are stacked on top of each other. The middle sheet is rotated clockwise \(30^\circ\) about its center and the top sheet is rotated clockwise \(60^\circ\) about its center, resulting in the \(24\)-sided polygon shown in the figure below.

The area of this polygon can be expressed in the form \(a-b\sqrt{c},\) where \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) are positive integers, and \(c\) is not divisible by the square of any prime. What is \(a+b+c?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-3)

A rectangle with side lengths \(1\) and \(3,\) a square with side length \(1,\) and a rectangle \(R\) are inscribed inside a larger square as shown. The sum of all possible values for the area of \(R\) can be written in the form \(\tfrac mn,\) where \(m\) and \(n\) are relatively prime positive integers. What is \(m+n?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-4)

As shown in the figure below, point \(E\) lies on the opposite half-plane determined by line \(CD\) from point \(A\) so that \(\angle CDE = 110^\circ.\) Point \(F\) lies on \(\overline{AD}\) so that \(DE = DF,\) and \(ABCD\) is a square. What is the degree measure of \(\angle AFE?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-5)

In the figure, equilateral hexagon \(ABCDEF\) has three nonadjacent acute interior angles that each measure \(30^\circ.\) The enclosed area of the hexagon is \(6\sqrt{3}.\) What is the perimeter of the hexagon?

[Figure 1](attached-image-6)

Let \(ABCD\) be an isosceles trapezoid with \(\overline{BC} \parallel \overline{AD}\) and \(AB = CD.\) Points \(X\) and \(Y\) lie on diagonal \(\overline{AC}\) with \(X\) between \(A\) and \(Y,\) as shown in the figure. Suppose \(\angle AXD = \angle BYC = 90^\circ,\) \(AX = 3,\) \(XY = 1,\) and \(YC = 2.\) What is the area of \(ABCD?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-7)

What is the area of the shaded figure shown below?

mappings.rationale: The square tops give parallel cross-sections of widths 3 and 2 at heights 3 and 5. Similar triangles relate these widths to the remaining heights, determining the triangle's base and area.
mappings.answerReason: If the triangle's height is h, then 3/(h-3)=2/(h-5), so h=9. Its base is 3·9/6=9/2, giving area (1/2)(9/2)(9)=81/4.

mappings.rationale: Finding the square's area requires recovering its side from the perpendicular crossing segments. Congruent right triangles give equal hypotenuses, after which altitude projection relations apply; coordinate orthogonality provides an alternative.
mappings.answerReason: Triangles ABP and BCQ are congruent, so CQ=BP=13. In right triangle BCQ, altitude BR=6 gives CR·RQ=36 and CR+RQ=13. Since BC>BQ, CR=9 and RQ=4. Thus BC²=CQ·CR=13·9=117.

mappings.rationale: The rotated squares produce repeated boundary pieces. Joining the common center to the polygon's vertices partitions the union into 24 congruent triangles, whose dimensions follow from 30° geometry.
mappings.answerReason: With the common center at the origin, one boundary edge runs from (3,3) to (√3,3). Each of the 24 congruent triangles therefore has base 3-√3 and height 3. The area is 24·3(3-√3)/2=108-36√3, so a+b+c=108+36+3=147.

mappings.rationale: The boundary contacts of the unit square and the 1-by-3 rectangle fix the outer square. Opposite sides and right angles of R then yield two admissible configurations, using either coordinate perpendicularity or similar corner triangles.
mappings.answerReason: The outer side is √10. After multiplying coordinates by √10 and placing the origin at the upper-left corner, the shared vertex of R is (4,3), and the long rectangle edge is 3y=x+11. Writing R's top vertex as (h,0), the rectangle conditions give (h-7)(h-8)=0. These yield actual areas 9/5 and 5/3, whose sum is 52/15. Thus m+n=67.

mappings.rationale: The square's right angle and the given exterior angle determine the vertex angle of isosceles triangle DFE. Its equal base angles and the opposite rays FA and FD determine the requested angle.
mappings.answerReason: At D, ∠FDE=360°-90°-110°=160°. Since DE=DF, ∠DFE=(180°-160°)/2=10°. Rays FA and FD are opposite, so ∠AFE=180°-10°=170°.

mappings.rationale: Joining B, D, and F partitions the concave hexagon into an equilateral central triangle and three congruent isosceles triangles with 30° apex angles. Their areas determine the common hexagon side length.
mappings.answerReason: Let each hexagon side be s. A perpendicular projection in a 30° ear triangle gives BF²=(2-√3)s². The total area is (√3/4)(2-√3)s²+3s²/4=(√3/2)s². Equating this to 6√3 gives s²=12, so the perimeter is 6s=12√3.

mappings.rationale: Parallel bases make right triangles AXD and CYB similar. Their altitude ratio, together with equal trapezoid legs and the Pythagorean theorem, determines the two heights above and below diagonal AC.
mappings.answerReason: Let BY=u and DX=v. Similarity gives v/u=3/2. Also AY=4 and CX=3, so AB=CD gives u²+16=v²+9. Hence u²=28/5, v²=63/5, and u+v=√35. Since AC=6, the area is 6(u+v)/2=3√35.

mappings.rationale: The grid supplies the vertices and heights. The shaded region is the large triangle minus the triangular notch sharing its base.
mappings.answerReason: The common base from (1,0) to (5,0) has length 4. The outer and removed triangles have heights 5 and 2, so the shaded area is (1/2)·4·5-(1/2)·4·2=6.
